name: Cadillac Mountain
summary: The highest headland on the eastern seaboard, and among the first places in the United States to catch the sunrise.

name: Jordan Pond
summary: A glacial tarn below the twin summits of the Bubbles, circled by a level shore path.

name: Thunder Hole
summary: A narrow inlet where an incoming swell slams air out of a sea cave with a boom.

name: Sand Beach
summary: A pocket of shell sand between granite headlands, in water that rarely passes 55°F.

name: Otter Cliff
summary: A 110-foot granite wall dropping straight into the Atlantic.

name: Bass Harbor Head Light
summary: An 1858 light station on the island's quiet south-western shore.

name: Schoodic Point
summary: The park's mainland section, where dark basalt dykes cut through pink granite ledges.

image.altText: Two women walking on a rocky shore with water and a mountain the backgound

name: Park Loop Road
summary: Twenty-seven miles threading the eastern side of Mount Desert Island, designed to reveal the coast a view at a time.

name: Acadia Gateway Center
summary: The Acadia Gateway Center is an intermodal transit and welcome center located on Route 3 in Trenton three miles north of Mount Desert Island. Facilities include an Island Explorer bus stop, day-use parking, and an 11,000-square-foot welcome center with tourism information, a store, waiting area, and restrooms.
hours: 8 am to 6 pm, Wed May 20 to Mon Oct 12, 2026

name: Hulls Cove Visitor Center
summary: Located close to Bar Harbor off Route 3, the Hulls Cove Visitor Center is Acadia’s main visitor contact station and transportation hub from May into October. It is a popular, and often crowded, first stop for many visitors.

name: Islesford Historical Museum
summary: The Islesford Historical Museum continues its mission of celebrating Islesford’s cultural history. Historical exhibits showcase life on and around Cranberry Isles from the 1700s to present.

name: Schoodic Institute Welcome Center at Rockefeller Hall
summary: The Schoodic Institute Welcome Center at Rockefeller Hall is located on Schoodic Peninsula off the one-way loop road. Exhibits about the old Navy base and park information can be found here.

name: Sieur de Monts Nature Center
summary: Sieur de Monts Nature Center has visitor services, hiking information, and interactive exhibits. It acts as a trailhead for many hiking trails starting in the Sieur de Monts area.

name: Winter Information: Bar Harbor Chamber of Commerce
summary: During winter and spring, information and sales of some passes are available at the Bar Harbor Chamber of Commerce, 2 Cottage Street, at the corner of Cottage and Main streets (GPS coordinates = 44.398633, -68.204933). The center is open 7 days a week from 8 am to 4 pm.

name: Blackwoods Campground
summary: Blackwoods Campground is located on the east side of Mount Desert Island, about 5 miles (8 km) south of Bar Harbor on Route 3.

name: Seawall Campground
summary: Seawall Campground is located on the west side of Mount Desert Island about 4 miles (6 km) south of Southwest Harbor.

name: Schoodic Woods Campground
summary: Schoodic Woods Campground is the newest campground in the park and located 1.5 miles (2.5 km) southeast of Winter Harbor on the Schoodic Peninsula.

name: Duck Harbor Campground
summary: Duck Harbor Campground is located on Isle au Haut, a rugged island off the coast of Stonington, Maine.

name: Mount Alava
summary: The ridge-top trail above Pago Pago Harbor, with the harbor on one side and the north coast falling away on the other.

image.caption: Mount Alava
image.altText: A lush group of mountains surrounded by ocean with a lakeside town nested in the mountain valley.

name: Vatia and Pola Island
summary: A north-coast village beneath the ridge, facing the sheer sea stack of Pola Island.

name: Ofu Beach
summary: A long white-sand beach on Ofu, with some of the clearest snorkelling in the territory over the reef.

name: Saua
summary: A site on Taʻū that Samoan tradition holds sacred, below forested cliffs.

image.caption: Sau well
image.altText: A close up picture of a well in the ground surrounded by mossy rocks.

name: Visitor Center and Park Store
summary: Open on weekdays from 8:00 am to 3:00 pm. Closed on weekends and federal holidays.
hours: Offering essential information, interactive exhibits, and a chance to learn about the park’s unique cultural and natural heritage, the visitor center provides an introduction to everything that makes this park special.

summary: Located at park headquarters, the Ben Reifel Visitor Center features exhibits, an air conditioned theater,and restroom facilities.

name: White River Visitor Center
summary: The visitor center is located on the Pine Ridge Reservation and offers a staffed information desk, exhibits, restrooms, picnic tables, and water. Impromptu talks are available by request.

name: Sage Creek Campground

name: Cedar Pass Campground
summary: Located near the Ben Reifel Visitor Center, the Cedar Pass Campground has 96 level sites with scenic views of the badlands formations.

name: Castolon Visitor Center
summary: Located in the Castolon Historic District, the Castolon Visitor Center is open daily during the winter months. River use permits are issued during normal business hours, and entrance fees can be paid at the Castolon Visitor Center.

name: Chisos Basin Visitor Center
summary: The Chisos Basin Visitor Center includes interactive exhibits on plants, animals, and birds found in the Chisos Mountains. Backcountry and river use permits are issued during normal business hours, and entrance fees can be paid at the visitor center.

name: Panther Junction Visitor Center
summary: Panther Junction Visitor Center is the best place to begin your visit. Backcountry & river use permits are issued here.

name: Persimmon Gap Visitor Center
summary: Persimmon Gap Visitor Center is located in a low pass between the Santiago Mountains at the northern entrance of the park. This pass has been a travel corridor for centuries for people entering and exiting the lower Big Bend country.

name: Rio Grande Village Visitor Center
summary: The Rio Grande Village Visitor Center is located 0.25 miles north of the Rio Grande Village developed area. New exhibits focus on the Rio Grande (how it has changed over time, how the NPS works with our Mexican counterparts to protect and care for it, and the rich assemblage of species that it supports).

name: Chisos Basin Campground
summary: The Chisos Basin Campground is nestled in an open woodland within a scenic mountain basin.

name: Rio Grande Village Campground
summary: Set in a grove of cottonwoods and acacia trees, the Rio Grande Village Campground is located near the Rio Grande.

name: Cottonwood Campground
summary: Cottonwood Campground is a quiet oasis in the western corner of Big Bend National Park.

name: Rio Grande Village RV
summary: Open, paved lot with grassy, tree-lined edges.

name: Boca Chita Key
summary: A small key with an ornamental lighthouse, a harbor and a campground, popular with boaters.

name: Elliott Key
summary: The park's largest island, with a campground, a harbor and a trail through tropical hardwood forest.

name: Maritime Heritage Trail
summary: Shipwrecks on the reef, including the Mandalay in shallow water — a snorkeler's wreck.

name: Fowey Rocks Lighthouse
summary: A cast-iron lighthouse standing on the reef, seen from boats offshore.

name: Stiltsville
summary: A cluster of houses on pilings in the bay, the last of a once-larger village.

name: Dante Fascell Visitor Center
summary: The Dante Fascell Visitor Center is located at Convoy Point, 9 miles East of the city of Homestead, Florida. A beautiful museum offers a virtual journey through the park's four ecosystems using dioramas, audio and video.

summary: Elliott Key campground is located on an island.

name: North Rim Ranger Station
summary: The North Rim Ranger Station is open intermittently in summer and closed in winter. In the summer, maps and information are available on the ranger station porch.

name: South Rim Visitor Center
summary: This visitor center has exhibits, information, book and map sales, water (available seasonally), vault toilets, and hiking trailheads. It is open year-round with the exception of Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day, and New Years Day.

name: South Rim Campground
summary: The South Rim Campground is located one mile (1.6 km) from the South Rim Visitor Center.

name: North Rim Campground
summary: The North Rim Campground is remote and has 13 sites dispersed among pinyon and juniper trees.

name: East Portal Campground
summary: East Portal Campground is located within Curecanti National Recreation Area, but is adjacent to and only accessible from Black Canyon National Park ($30 entrance fee).

name: Bryce Canyon Visitor Center
summary: The Bryce Canyon Visitor Center might be one of your first stops when visiting Bryce Canyon National Park. Here you can obtain driving and hiking directions beyond those available on this website, weather forecasts, a current schedule of Park Ranger guided programs, Junior Ranger booklets, and information on area services including lodging, dining and other attractions.

name: North Campground

name: Canyonlands Backcountry Office
summary: The central backcountry office is located at park administrative offices south of Moab. Rangers can answer questions about backcountry travel over phone or email and issue permits online.
hours: Rangers are normally available five days a week to answer questions over the phone or email and issue permits online.

name: Hans Flat Ranger Station
summary: The remote Hans Flat (Maze) Ranger Station is normally open daily year-round. This ranger contact station has a picnic table and vault toilet, and a small selection of books and maps for sale.

name: Island in the Sky Visitor Center
summary: The Island in the Sky Visitor Center offers exhibits, book & map sales, park orientation film, backcountry permits, general information, vault toilets, and park rangers on duty. You can get drinking water inside (during open hours) or outside (24 hours a day) during summer and fall.

name: The Needles Visitor Center
summary: The Needles Visitor Center normally offers exhibits, book & map sales, backcountry permits, information, picnic area, and park rangers on duty. The park orientation movie (15 minutes) is available on demand.

name: The Needles Campground
summary: The Needles Campground has 26 individual sites.

name: Island in the Sky (Willow Flat) Campground
summary: Island in the Sky Campground (Willow Flat) has 12 sites, first-come, first-served.

name: The Needles District Group Campsites
summary: The Needles district has three group campsites in different locations, which can accommodate up to 15, 25, or 50 campers (respectively).

name: Capitol Reef National Park Visitor Center
summary: Capitol Reef National Park visitor center sits at the intersection of UT-24 and the Scenic Drive.

name: Group Campsite
summary: The Group Campsite is a secluded site located near the Fruita Campground and can accommodate a maximum of 40 people.

name: Fruita Campground
summary: The 71 site Fruita campground is the only developed campground in the park, offering picnic tables, fire rings, restrooms, water and a dump station.

name: Inspiration Point
summary: The view west along Anacapa's chain of islets, with Santa Cruz beyond.

name: Scorpion Ranch
summary: The landing on Santa Cruz, with an old ranch, a campground and trails up onto the cliffs.

name: Potato Harbor
summary: A cove below sheer cliffs, reached on a walk from Scorpion Anchorage.

name: Cavern Point
summary: A loop over Santa Cruz's sea cliffs, good for spotting whales in season.

name: Painted Cave
summary: One of the largest sea caves in the world, on Santa Cruz's north shore, seen by kayak or boat.

name: Torrey Pines
summary: A grove of one of the rarest pines in the country, on Santa Rosa's east coast.

name: Point Bennett
summary: San Miguel's western tip, where tens of thousands of seals and sea lions haul out.

name: Channel Islands National Park Visitor Center
summary: The Robert J. Lagomarsino Visitor Center at Channel Islands National Park features a bookstore, a display of marine aquatic life, and exhibits featuring the unique character of each park island.

name: Outdoors Santa Barbara Visitor Center
summary: The small Outdoors Santa Barbara Visitor Center not only has one of the best views of Santa Barbara, but also offers visitors information about Channel Islands National Park, Channel Islands National Marine Sanctuary, Santa Barbara Maritime Museum, and the City of Santa Barbara. Open 10:30 am until 4:30 pm daily.

name: San Miguel Island Ranger and Visitor Contact Station
summary: The visitor contact and ranger station is only open when staff is present.

name: Santa Barbara Island Visitor Center
summary: A small visitor center is located on the island. Features include displays on the natural and cultural resources of the island.

name: Santa Rosa Island Visitor Contact Station
summary: The historic schoolhouse is now home to this small visitor contact station with exhibits on the ranching history of Santa Rosa Island.

name: Scorpion Ranch Visitor Center on Santa Cruz Island
summary: The small visitor center resides in the historic Scorpion Ranch house which was constructed in 1886-1887.

name: Visitor Center Anacapa Island
summary: Once the historic Coast Guard general services building (workshop and garage), this Mission Revival style building now serves as a small visitor center that features include displays on the natural and cultural resources of the island and the original lead-crystal Fresnel lens from the Anacapa Lighthouse.

name: Anacapa Island Campground
summary: Primitive camping is available (seven sites; $15 per night per site; reservations required).

name: Scorpion Canyon Campground
summary: Primitive camping is available (25 individual sites at $15 per night-per site and 6 group sites at $40 per night-per site; reservations required).

name: Del Norte Backcountry Campground
summary: The Santa Cruz Island Del Norte Backcountry Campground is currently the only backcountry campground on Santa Cruz Island.

name: Water Canyon Campground
summary: Primitive camping is available (15 sites; $15 per night per site; reservations required).

name: Santa Rosa Island Backcountry Beach Camping
summary: Backcountry camping on Santa Rosa Island is currently limited to certain beaches between August 15th and December 31st.

name: San Miguel Island Campground
summary: Primitive camping is available (nine sites; $15 per night per site; reservations required).

name: Santa Barbara Island Campground
summary: Primitive camping is available (seven sites; $15 per night per site; reservations required).

name: Boardwalk Loop
summary: A 2.6-mile raised boardwalk through old-growth bottomland forest and past cypress knees, from the visitor center.

name: Weston Lake
summary: An oxbow lake on the Weston Lake Loop, with cypress growing in the water.

name: Cedar Creek
summary: A blackwater creek through the forest, followed by a marked canoe and kayak trail.

name: Harry Hampton Visitor Center
summary: Open 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. daily. Closed New Year's Day, Washington's Birthday, Columbus Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day.

name: Longleaf Campground
summary: The Longleaf Campground offers walk up campsites for visitors wishing to camp in the frontcountry of Congaree.

name: Bluff Campground
summary: The Bluff Campground is a hike in campground and is perfect for those looking to camp in the frontcountry yet have a more backcountry experience.

name: Maltese Cross Cabin
summary: Roosevelt's first ranch cabin, moved to sit behind the South Unit Visitor Center in Medora.

image.caption: Theodore Roosevelt's Maltese Cross Cabin
image.altText: A log cabin sits in a grassy area. Trees and a fence are visible behind it, and a sidewalk in front.

name: Wind Canyon
summary: A short trail to a bluff above the Little Missouri, with wind-sculpted sandstone. Good at sunset.

image.caption: A view from Wind Canyon
image.altText: A view down Wind Canyon toward the river. Green trees line a grassy trail at the bottom.

name: Buck Hill
summary: A short climb to one of the highest points in the South Unit.

image.caption: View from Buck Hill
image.altText: A view looking down into a deep valley, with small buttes topped by dark trees.

name: Prairie dog town
summary: A pull-off beside a busy black-tailed prairie dog colony on the South Unit's scenic drive.

name: Coal Vein Trail
summary: A short loop where a lignite seam burned for years, leaving scoria and collapsed ground.

image.caption: Coal Vein Guided Hike Trailhead
image.altText: A trailhead sign. Behind it, buttes rise against a blue sky, and grass and sage grow on the ground.

name: Elkhorn Ranch
summary: The site of Roosevelt's home ranch; only the foundation stones remain. Reached by gravel road.

image.caption: Elkhorn Ranch Cabin Site
image.altText: A view of a grassy field, with junipers in the background, as well as a butte under a blue sky.

name: River Bend Overlook
summary: A North Unit viewpoint with a stone shelter built by the Civilian Conservation Corps.

image.caption: River Bend Overlook
image.altText: A small stone shelter with a low pitched roof stands at the edge of a butte overlooking a river.

name: Oxbow Overlook
summary: The end of the North Unit's scenic drive, above a bend of the Little Missouri.

image.caption: Oxbow Overlook
image.altText: A river meanders through cottonwood trees and steep buttes.

name: Caprock Coulee
summary: A North Unit loop past caprock formations and through a coulee.

name: North Unit Visitor Center
summary: A small visitor center is located at the park entrance for visitors to the North Unit. Speak with a ranger, receive assistance with any trip planning needs, obtain a backcountry permit, purchase a souvenir at the bookstore, or watch the park film, Refuge of the American Spirit.

name: Painted Canyon Visitor Center
summary: Features: Panoramic views, wildlife viewing, hiking trails, staffed information desk, exhibits and displays, gift shop, picnic shelters, drinking fountain, vending machines, public telephone, and restrooms are wheelchair accessible.

name: South Unit Visitor Center
summary: Rangers staff the desk, assist visitors with trip planning, and issue backcountry permits. Theodore Roosevelt's Maltese Cross Cabin, located just outside, is open for self-guided tours year-round.

name: Cottonwood Campground
summary: Cottonwood Campground lies inside the park, about 5 miles from Medora, ND.

name: Juniper Campground
summary: Juniper Campground is 5 miles from Hwy 85 and is the only campground in the park's North Unit.

name: Roundup Group Horse Camp
summary: Roundup is the park's only camping facility in which horses are permitted.

name: Trunk Bay
summary: A famous white-sand beach with an underwater snorkelling trail along its reef. An amenity fee is charged.

name: Cinnamon Bay
summary: A long, wide north-shore beach with the park's campground and a nature trail past plantation ruins.

name: Maho Beach
summary: A calm, shallow bay where sea turtles often graze on seagrass.

name: Francis Bay
summary: A quiet bay for snorkelling, with a short trail past a salt pond good for birds.

name: Hawksnest Beach
summary: A small beach close to Cruz Bay, with reefs just offshore.

name: Honeymoon Beach
summary: A beach reached on foot by the Lind Point Trail from Cruz Bay.

name: Salt Pond Bay
summary: A sheltered south-shore bay and the start of the trail to Ram Head.

name: Annaberg Sugar Plantation
summary: The partly restored ruins of a sugar factory and windmill, with views toward Tortola.

name: Reef Bay Trail
summary: A steep trail down through forest to Taíno petroglyphs and a sugar mill. The climb back is hard.

name: Cruz Bay Visitor Center
summary: Visitor and Information Center for Virgin Islands National Park and Virgin Islands Coral Reef National Monument.

name: Cinnamon Bay Beach and Campground
summary: The campground offers bare tent sites, eco-tents, and cottages.

name: Kettle Falls Hotel
summary: A historic hotel reached by boat, between Namakan and Rainy Lakes — one of the few places in the lower 48 where you look south into Canada.

name: Ellsworth Rock Gardens
summary: Terraced gardens and rock sculptures built by a summer resident on Kabetogama Lake.

name: Grassy Bay Cliffs
summary: Sheer rock walls rising from Sand Point Lake, seen by boat.

name: Hoist Bay
summary: The site of a logging camp on Namakan Lake, where logs were rafted until 1929.

name: Harry Oveson Fish Camp
summary: A preserved commercial fishing camp on Kabetogama Lake.

name: Rainy Lake
summary: The park's largest lake, shared with Canada, with the main visitor center at its western end.

name: Kabetogama Lake
summary: A lake on the peninsula's south side, with resorts and a visitor center on its shore.

name: Ash River Visitor Center
summary: The Ash River Visitor Center is open during our summer season from late May to late September. Ash River Visitor Center is closed over the winter season.

name: Crane Lake Visitor Center
summary: Located in the town of Crane Lake, the newest visitor center at Voyageurs National Park features an exhibit area, seating, an information desk, and a conference room for viewing the park film. Just next door is the Crane Lake Voyageur RV Park and Campground, offering convenient access to water activities and outdoor adventures.

name: Kabetogama Lake Visitor Center
summary: Nestled along the southwest shoreline of Kabetogama Lake, the visitor center is in the small community of Kabetogama. The Kabetogama Lake Visitor Center is open during our summer season from late May to late September and is closed through the winter.

name: Rainy Lake Visitor Center
summary: The closest visitor center to International Falls, the Rainy Lake Visitor Center hours of operation vary with the season. The visitor center offers an exhibit area, displays, a bookstore, a staffed information desk, a children's activity table, and a theater for viewing the park film.

name: Dunes Drive
summary: An eight-mile road from the visitor center into the heart of the dunes; the last miles are packed gypsum, ploughed like snow.

image.caption: End of Pavement
image.altText: The pavement's end on Dunes Drive.

name: Interdune Boardwalk
summary: An accessible boardwalk across the sparse plants between the dunes.

image.caption: Interdune Boardwalk
image.altText: A visitor walking down the Interdune Boardwalk.

name: Dune Life Nature Trail
summary: A short loop with signs on the animals that live in the dunes.

name: Alkali Flat Trail
summary: A five-mile loop over open dunes to the edge of the dry bed of ancient Lake Otero. Follow the marker posts closely.

name: Playa Trail
summary: An easy walk to a playa, a shallow basin that fills with water after rain.

name: Sledding dunes
summary: Steep dune faces for sledding. Waxed plastic saucers are sold at the park store.

name: White Sands Visitor Center
summary: The visitor center was built in 1936 and is part of the historic district at White Sands. Inside you will find the park store as well as the museum for the park.

name: Backcountry Camping
summary: Due to rehabilitation of camping sites, backcountry camping is closed.

name: Rankin Ridge
summary: A short loop to a fire tower at one of the highest points in the park, with views over the Black Hills and plains.

name: Prairie Vista Nature Trail
summary: An easy walk from the visitor center onto the prairie.

name: Elk Mountain Nature Trail
summary: A loop from the campground where prairie meets ponderosa pine forest.

name: Wind Cave Canyon
summary: An easy walk down a limestone canyon, good for birds such as cliff swallows and owls.

name: Cold Brook Canyon
summary: A trail down a canyon to the prairie and a prairie dog town.

name: Centennial Trail
summary: The southern end of a long trail through the Black Hills, crossing bison country.

name: Wind Cave Visitor Center
summary: The visitor center is open daily except for Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Year's Days. All cave tours are ranger-led and leave from the visitor center.

name: Elk Mountain Campground
summary: This 64-site campground is open year round.

name: Kennecott Mines
summary: The red mill town of the copper mines, with ranger-led and guided tours of the fourteen-storey concentration mill.

image.caption: Kennecott Mines
image.altText: Kennecott Mines National Historic Landmark

name: Root Glacier
summary: A trail from Kennecott to the edge of the glacier. Walking on the ice needs crampons, or a guide.

image.caption: Root Glacier
image.altText: Root Glacier

name: McCarthy Road
summary: Sixty miles of gravel from Chitina along an old railbed, ending at a footbridge to McCarthy.

image.caption: McCarthy Road Information Station
image.altText: McCarthy Road Information Station

name: Nabesna Road
summary: A 42-mile gravel road into the park's northern foothills, with trails, campsites and views of the Wrangells.

name: Crystalline Hills Trail
summary: A short hike off the McCarthy Road with views of the Chugach and Wrangell mountains.

image.caption: Crystalline Hills Trail
image.altText: Crystalline Hills Trail

name: Malaspina Glacier
summary: The largest piedmont glacier in North America, best seen from the air or from Yakutat.

image.caption: Malaspina Glacier
image.altText: Malaspina Glacier

name: Mount Saint Elias
summary: The park's highest summit, on the Canadian border, rising from near sea level to 18,008 feet.

name: Mount Wrangell
summary: A huge, gently sloped shield volcano whose summit vents still steam.

name: Chitina Ranger Station
summary: Located in downtown Chitina at mile 33 on the Edgerton Highway. Upon entering Chitina town southbound, turn left at the Chitina Hotel, drive down the gravel road 0.2 mile (300 meters), station on left.

name: Kennecott Visitor Center
summary: Located in the "Blackburn School," the Kennecott Visitor Center has exhibits and Rangers available to help with your trip planning.

name: Slana Ranger Station
summary: Get the latest Nabesna Road conditions and information about its recreational opportunities.

name: Wrangell-St. Elias Visitor Center in Copper Center
summary: Enjoy the exhibits, view the park film, hike nature trails, shop in the bookstore, gather park & area information, conduct backcountry trip planning, and view the large 3-D interactive map display. Park rangers provide guided talks and walks daily during the summer months.

name: Yakutat
summary: Yakutat is located in the southern portion of the park along the coastline in Yakutat Bay at the base of the St. Elias Mountains.

name: Kendesnii Campground
summary: Located on the Nabesna Road, this free camping area is the only National Park Service campground in Wrangell-St.

name: Old Faithful
summary: The park's most predictable large geyser, erupting every 60 to 110 minutes to around 130 feet.

name: Grand Prismatic Spring
summary: The largest hot spring in the United States, ringed in orange and green by heat-loving microbial mats.

image.caption: Grand Prismatic Spring
image.altText: Steam rises off of a large, blue hot spring surrounded by yellow, orange, and brown microbial mats.

name: Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone
summary: Twenty miles of canyon cut through hydrothermally altered rock, with two major waterfalls.

name: Mammoth Hot Springs
summary: Travertine terraces built and abandoned as spring vents shift, sometimes within a season.

name: Lamar Valley
summary: Open sage grassland where bison, elk and wolves are most reliably seen at dawn and dusk.

name: Hayden Valley
summary: A broad former lakebed along the Yellowstone River, grazed by bison herds.

name: Norris Geyser Basin
summary: The park's hottest and most changeable basin, and home to Steamboat Geyser.

name: Yellowstone Lake
summary: The largest high-elevation lake in North America, sitting partly inside the caldera.

image.caption: Yellowstone Lake
image.altText: Sun rising over the waters of Yellowstone Lake.

name: Tower Fall
summary: A 132-foot fall dropping between volcanic pinnacles into the Yellowstone River.

name: Albright Visitor Center
summary: Here you can gather park information, orient yourself to the rest of the park (including road conditions, and campground and lodge availability), shop for souvenirs, explore exhibits to learn more about the wildlife and history of Yellowstone, join a ranger program, pick up a fishing permit (fees are payable by debit or credit card), or use the restrooms.

name: Canyon Visitor Education Center
summary: Stop by the Canyon Visitor Education Center to learn more about the geologic story of the area, including the Yellowstone volcano, and view a room-size relief map of Yellowstone. You can also get orientation information, pick up a fishing permit (fees are payable by debit or credit card), shop for a souvenir, find out what ranger programs are available, watch a 20-minute film, or use the restrooms.

name: Fishing Bridge Visitor Center and Trailside Museum
summary: The distinctive stone-and-log architecture of this old building—known as "parkitecture"—was one of several prototypes for park buildings around the country. Today, the visitor center and museum highlight the ecology of Yellowstone Lake, focusing on birds.

name: Grant Visitor Center
summary: Fire plays an important, natural role in the ecosystems found in Yellowstone National Park and the surrounding region. Learn more about this and the fires of 1988 in the exhibit hall, gather park information and trip ideas, shop for souvenirs at the park store, join a ranger program, buy a fishing, boating, or backcountry camping permit (fees are payable by debit or credit card), or use the restrooms.

name: Madison Information Station and Trailside Museum
summary: Located about halfway between Old Faithful and West Yellowstone, you can stop here for park information as visitors have been doing since 1930. The structure is an example of "parkitecture" or designing a building in a way that reflects the surrounding ecosystem.

name: Museum of the National Park Ranger
summary: Once a US Army outpost built in 1908, this visitor center houses exhibits that celebrate the history of the park ranger profession. The current structure replaced previous structures dating back to 1884.

name: Norris Geyser Basin Museum and Information Station
summary: Situated on the ridge overlooking the Norris Geyser Basin, this historic building is staffed during the summer with rangers who provide park information and facilitate ranger programs. Visitors have been seeking information here since 1930 when the museum was built as a "trailside museum" to serve people traveling in their own automobiles without a guide.

name: Old Faithful Visitor Education Center
summary: Located near Old Faithful Geyser, this visitor center offers views of the geyser's eruption from the tall, windowed front of the visitor center. Additionally, you can gather park information, talk with a park ranger at the front desk, shop for souvenirs in the park store, delve into the natural wonders of Yellowstone in the exhibit hall, join a ranger program, or use the restrooms.

name: West Thumb Information Station
summary: This facility is closed until further notice as of July 2026. A small facility at the start of the West Thumb Geyser Basin boardwalks, where you can visit with a park ranger and gather park information, shop for souvenirs in the park store, or join a ranger program.

name: West Yellowstone Visitor Information Center (Chamber of Commerce Desk)
summary: Located in the town of West Yellowstone, Montana, there is a desk staffed by National Park Service rangers (summer and winters only). The building is open year-round and a second desk is staffed by the West Yellowstone Chamber of Commerce.

name: West Yellowstone Visitor Information Center (NPS Desk)
summary: Located in the town of West Yellowstone, Montana, there is a desk and backcountry office staffed by National Park Service rangers (summer and winters only). The building is open year-round and a second desk is staffed by the West Yellowstone Chamber of Commerce.

name: Canyon Campground
summary: Canyon Campground—elevation 7,900 feet (2408 m)—lies in a lodgepole pine forest at Canyon Village, south of the Washburn range and near the breath-taking Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone River.

name: Bridge Bay Campground
summary: Bridge Bay Campground—elevation 7,800 feet (2377 m)—is located near Yellowstone Lake, one of the largest, high-elevation, fresh-water lakes in North America.

name: Fishing Bridge RV Park
summary: Fishing Bridge RV Park—elevation 7,800 feet (2377 m)—is located near the Yellowstone River where it exits Yellowstone Lake on its way toward the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone.

name: Grant Village Campground
summary: Grant Campground—elevation 7,800 feet (2377 m)—is located in Grant Village, just off the Grand Loop Road at the south end of Yellowstone Lake.

name: Madison Campground
summary: Madison Campground—elevation 6,800 feet (2073 m)—sits about 14 miles east from the town of West Yellowstone and 16 miles north of Old Faithful.

name: Indian Creek Campground
summary: Located about eight miles south of Mammoth Hot Springs on the road to Norris, Indian Creek Campground—elevation 7,300 feet (2225 m)—sits near the base of the Gallatin Mountains and offers breathtaking views of Electric Peak.

name: Mammoth Campground
summary: The only campground in the park open year-round, Mammoth Campground—elevation 6,200 feet (1890 m)—is located five miles south of the park's North Entrance.

name: Norris Campground
summary: Norris Campground will remain closed for the foreseeable future.

name: Pebble Creek Campground
summary: Pebble Creek Campground was significantly impacted by the 2022 floods and will remain CLOSED until further notice for flood recovery work.

name: Tower Fall Campground
summary: Tower Fall Campground—elevation 6,600 feet (2012 m)—is located on the north side of the steep, winding, road to Dunraven Pass.

name: Lewis Lake Campground
summary: Lewis Lake Campground—elevation 7,800 ft (2377 m)—is about eight miles from the South Entrance and a short walk from the southeast shore of Lewis Lake.

name: Slough Creek Campground
summary: Near some of the best wildlife watching opportunities in the park.

name: Tunnel View
summary: The classic view up the valley to El Capitan, Bridalveil Fall and Half Dome.

image.caption: Tunnel View
image.altText: Large granite monoliths in the distance with a dense conifer forest below

name: Yosemite Falls
summary: A short loop to the base of the lower fall. The falls run strongest in late spring and are often dry by late summer.

name: El Capitan
summary: A sheer granite monolith; from the meadow, look for climbers on the face.

name: Half Dome
summary: The park's emblem. The hike to the top, with its final climb up steel cables, needs a permit.

name: Glacier Point
summary: An overlook 3,200 feet above the valley, facing Half Dome, reached by road in summer.

name: Bridalveil Fall
summary: A short walk to the foot of a waterfall that flows all year.

name: Mirror Lake
summary: A seasonal lake below Half Dome, fullest in spring.

name: Sentinel Dome and Taft Point
summary: Two easy walks off Glacier Point Road: a granite dome and a cliff-edge overlook.

name: Mariposa Grove
summary: The park's largest sequoia grove, near the South Entrance, with the Grizzly Giant.

name: Tuolumne Meadows
summary: A broad subalpine meadow on the Tioga Road, ringed by granite domes.

name: Tenaya Lake
summary: A high-country lake with a sandy beach, beside the Tioga Road.

name: Hetch Hetchy
summary: A reservoir in a valley once compared to Yosemite's, with trails to Wapama Falls.

name: Big Oak Flat Information Station
summary: The Big Oak Flat Information Station has an information desk, wilderness permit desk, and Yosemite Conservancy bookstore. In the winter, self-registration wilderness permits for the Crane Flat area and Tioga Road trailheads only, are available on the front porch.

name: Tuolumne Meadows Visitor Center
summary: The Tuolumne Meadows Visitor Center has an information desk, Yosemite Conservancy bookstore, and an exhibit area detailing the area's geology, plant and animal life, and history. A designated accessible parking space and entrance are available.

name: Wawona Visitor Center at Hill's Studio
summary: The Wawona Visitor Center has an information desk, wilderness permit desk, and Yosemite Conservancy bookstore. It includes an exhibit of Thomas Hill’s work, recreating a "salon hanging"—paintings covering the wall from floor to ceiling, typical of Victorian galleries in the nineteenth century.

name: Yosemite Valley Welcome Center
summary: The Yosemite Valley Welcome Center is the destination for visitor information in Yosemite Valley. The welcome center has an information desk, informational exhibits, and a Yosemite Conservancy bookstore.

name: Upper Pines Campground
summary: Upper Pines is located near the Merced River in Yosemite Valley.

name: Hodgdon Meadow Campground
summary: Hodgdon Meadow Campground is conveniently located along the Big Oak Flat Road at the Big Oak Flat Entrance.

name: North Pines Campground
summary: North Pines is located along the Merced River in Yosemite Valley.

name: Lower Pines Campground
summary: Lower Pines is located along the Merced River in Yosemite Valley.

name: Wawona Campground
summary: The Wawona Campground is located along the South Fork Merced River close to historic Wawona.

name: Tuolumne Meadows Campground
summary: Tuolumne Meadows Campground is Yosemite’s largest, and is located along the Tioga Road, with some areas located near the Tuolumne River.

name: Crane Flat Campground
summary: The Crane Flat Campground is located along the Big Oak Flat Road, just west of Crane Flat, about 30 minutes northwest of Yosemite Valley, at 6,200 ft (1,900 m) elevation.

name: Camp 4 Campground
summary: Camp 4 is located in Yosemite Valley near the base of granite cliffs close to Yosemite Falls.

name: White Wolf Campground
summary: White Wolf Campground is located off the Tioga Road between Tuolumne Meadows and Crane Flat, approximately an hour from Yosemite Valley at 8,000 feet (2,400 m).

name: Porcupine Flat Campground
summary: Porcupine Flat Campground is located off the Tioga Road about 30 minutes west of Tuolumne Meadows and over an hour from Yosemite Valley.

name: Yosemite Creek Campground
summary: Yosemite Creek Campground is located nearly 5 miles off the Tioga Road (via a rough unpaved road) 26 miles west of Tuolumne Meadows, and a little over an hour from Yosemite Valley.

name: Tamarack Flat Campground
summary: Tamarack Flat Campground is located off the Tioga Road just east of Crane Flat.

name: Bridalveil Creek Campground
summary: The Bridalveil Creek Campground is located along the Glacier Point Road near Bridalveil Creek and is surrounded by a beautiful forest of red fir and lodgepole pine.

name: Wawona Horse Camp
summary: The Wawona Horse Camp is located along the South Fork Merced River adjacent to historic Wawona.

name: Tuolumne Meadows Horse Camp
summary: Tuolumne Meadows Horse Campsites are located within Tuolumne Meadows Campground along the Tioga Road.

name: Bridalveil Creek Horse Camp
summary: The Bridalveil Creek Horse Camp is within Bridalveil Creek Campground located along the Glacier Point Road near Bridalveil Creek and surrounded by a beautiful forest of red fir and lodgepole pine.

name: Angels Landing
summary: A fin of Navajo sandstone reached by switchbacks and a chained ridge, 1,500 feet above the canyon floor.

name: The Narrows
summary: The Virgin River's slot canyon, in places twenty feet wide between thousand-foot walls. Walked in the river itself.

name: Observation Point
summary: The canyon's highest viewpoint, looking down on Angels Landing.

name: Emerald Pools
summary: Three stepped pools fed by seeps and a hanging garden of ferns.

name: Court of the Patriarchs
summary: Three sandstone peaks named for Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

image.caption: Court of the Patriarchs
image.altText: Photo of three large sandstone mountains above a shuttle bus.

name: Weeping Rock
summary: An alcove where water that fell as rain centuries ago seeps from the rock face.

image.caption: Weeping Rock
image.altText: Two people sit in a rock alcove, with water dripping off the overhang in front of them.

name: Canyon Overlook
summary: A short walk off the Zion–Mount Carmel Highway to a ledge above Pine Creek.

name: Kolob Canyons
summary: The park's quiet north-west corner: red finger canyons cut into the Kolob Terrace.

name: Human History Museum
summary: Immerse yourself in the human history of Zion National Park! Rangers staff an information desk during operating hours.

name: Kolob Canyons Visitor Center
summary: Closed daily from 12pm-1pm This is the entry point to the Kolob Canyons area of the park. It is located 45 miles north of Springdale and 17 miles south of Cedar City at Exit 40 on Interstate 15.

name: Zion Canyon Visitor Center
summary: Located near the South Entrance of the park, the Zion Canyon Visitor Center is an excellent place to begin your exploration of Zion Canyon. Park rangers and outdoor exhibits will help you plan your visit and make the most of your time.

name: Zion Nature Center
summary: During the summer, come visit the Zion Nature Center! This is a perfect place to learn about geology, animals, and the history of Zion.

name: Watchman Campground
summary: Watchman Campground is located next to the Zion Canyon Visitor Center, ¼ mile away from the South Entrance in Springdale, Utah.

name: South Campground
summary: South Campground is located between the Zion Canyon Visitor Center and Zion Nature Center, ½ mile from the South Entrance in Springdale, Utah.

name: Lava Point Campground
summary: Lava Point Campground is open as weather allows, typically from May through September.

name: Knob Creek Tavern Visitor Center
summary: Located at the Kentucky Boyhood Home at Knob Creek Unit.

name: Visitor Center at Abraham Lincoln Birthplace
summary: The Visitor Center at the Birthplace Unit is open 9:00 am - 5:00 pm eastern time. Inside there are exhibits, including the Lincoln family Bible, a 15 minute long movie, Abraham Lincoln: The Kentucky Years, and the park store.

name: Adams National Historical Park Visitor Center
summary: The Visitor Center is located at 1250 Hancock Street in the heart of downtown Quincy. From May 1 to October 31, the Visitor Center is open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
hours: The Visitor Center is open 11:00 am to 4:00 pm Mondays through Fridays.

name: African Burial Ground National Monument Visitor Center
summary: The visitor center is located at 290 Broadway, mid-block on Broadway between Duane and Reade Streets. It contains a self-guided museum, a theater that plays the 20-minute park film "Our Time At Last," restrooms, a gift store, a water fountain, and a staffed information desk.

name: Agate Fossil Beds National Monument Visitor Center
summary: The visitor center is open every day except Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Years Day. Summer hours are May 15 through September 30.

name: King Salmon Visitor Center
summary: Located next door to the King Salmon Airport, the King Salmon Visitor Center provides information on the many federal public lands of Southwest Alaska, particularly those in the Bristol Bay area. A large collection of films is available for viewing and an Alaska Geographic bookstore sells maps, charts, videos, posters, clothing and more.

name: Dock Ranger Station
summary: The ranger station at the Alcatraz Island Dock is staffed at all times. Staff here can help you with directions, information, Special Ranger and Junior Ranger programs, emergency assistance, and more.
hours: Just off the ferry from San Francisco, the Dock Ranger Station is where you can get information about Alcatraz Island.

name: Aleutian World War II National Historic Area Visitor Center
summary: The visitor center for Aleutian Islands World War II National Historic Area is located on Amaknak Island, a nearby island easily accessible from the major town of Unalaska.

name: Alibates Visitor Center
summary: The Alibates Visitor Center is home to exhibits, a theater and outdoor gardens, showcasing the history of Alibates Flint. It is also the meeting place for ranger-led hikes and tours of the monument, demonstrations, and numerous special events throughout the year.

name: Summit Level Visitor Center
summary: Located immediately off of US Route 22 at the Gallitzin Exit, this is the best place to start your tour. The Visitor Center has a 20-minute orientation movie shown on demand, interactive exhibits, and a bookstore.
hours: The Visitor Center, Engine House No. 6 Exhibit Shelter and the Lemon House are closed on Wednesdays and Thursdays.

name: Amistad National Recreation Area Visitor Center
summary: The Visitor Center offers several park-related movies. _Transparent Border_ is the park's official movie about how the reservoir came to influence a relationship between the US city of Del Rio and Mexico's Ciudad Acuña. It is available in English and español and is 35 minutes long.

name: The American Memorial Park Visitor Center and Pacific Historic Parks Bookstore
summary: The American Memorial Park Visitor Center is open on Tuesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday at 9:00 am to 4:00 pm.
hours: The American Memorial Park Visitor Center is open on Tuesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday at 9:00 am to 4:00 pm.

name: National Prisoner of War Museum
summary: At the National Prisoner of War Museum, the story of American prisoners of war (POWs) is powerfully presented through exhibits, audio-visual displays, and historic artifacts. The museum serves as the park's visitor center.

name: King Salmon Visitor Center
summary: Located next door to the King Salmon Airport, the King Salmon Visitor Center provides information on the many federal public lands of Southwest Alaska, particularly those in the Bristol Bay area. A large collection of films is available for viewing and an Alaska Geographic bookstore sells maps, charts, videos, posters, clothing, souvenirs, and more.

name: Andrew Johnson NHS Visitor Center
summary: Begin your visit to the Andrew Johnson National Historic Site at the Visitor Center. Here you will receive orientation to the other parts of the park, in addition to general information, brochures, and directions.

name: Antietam National Battlefield Visitor Center
summary: The park visitor center is a great place to begin your visit. We have a film that runs every 1/2 hour, small museum, book store, and restrooms.

name: Appomattox Court House Visitor Center
summary: The visitor center is located inside the reconstructed Appomattox Courthouse. It offers restroom facilities, visitor information and guidance, a 17-minute film, and exhibits focused on the history of Appomattox Court House.

name: Bayfield Headquarters
summary: The park's headquarters is located in the Bayfield, WI in the old Bayfield Courthouse Building. This iconic, brownstone building is easy to recognize from Washington Ave.

name: Little Sand Bay Visitor Center
summary: The Little Sand Bay Visitor Center will be closed throughout 2026 due to construction associated with the Little Sand Bay Marina Rehabilitation Project. We appreciate your patience as we work to improve infrastructure and visitor access.

name: Arkansas Post Visitor Center
summary: View the park movie, "Arkansas Post: Echoes of the Past" and explore museum exhibits reflecting over three hundred years of human history at Arkansas Post.
hours: The Arkansas Post Visitor Center and Museum is open Thursday to Monday and closed Tuesday to Wednesday.

name: Assateague Island Visitor Center
